reviewer_continuity: Same reviewer's continued original-rulebook challenge; this is not a new fresh independent vote or an additional saturation pass.
assignment_scope: Adjudicate three original p5 printed-component eligibility/timing candidates against the actual160 literal questions, using own prior complete rulebook/questions readings and the candidate08 Q146 delta.

source_basis.reuse: Hash-identical complete prior readings reused with explicit delivery ledger. Script confirms all159 other question objects unchanged and only Q146 changed. Current Q146 delta was delivered completely.

actual_question_version.Q146: Using the classic Filch Wild flare, what items may you illicitly take and from which locations, where may the retrieved ships go, when must the flare be revealed and when may it be zapped, what happens if caught, and what changes about the deck/discards after it is revealed?

adjudications.accepted_scope: The Wild cheating action's actor eligibility and use-phase permission, together as one bounded addition to its existing effect question.

primary_references.section: Classic Edition Filch flare illustration — Wild portion and its role/timing fields

primary_references.source_text: The timing strip along the bottom of each alien sheet and all non-encounter cards generally states when the component's game effect may be used.

adjudications.positive_original_base_applicability: The original p5 Classic Edition Filch Wild illustration itself supplies both fields and the illicit-taking action. Standard setup permits choosing the classic Filch flare as the single Filch version (p6). This needs no expansion, Technology or copied-power enabler.

coverage_comparison.finding: Current Q146 asks illicit items and their sources, retrieved-ship destination, when to reveal, when the flare may be zapped, caught penalty and pile placement. It does not ask which roles may perform the cheating action or in which phases the action itself is permitted. Reveal/catch/Zap timing is a different event from the hidden taking action's eligible use phase.

Clone Wild's As Any Player / Any Phase permission concerns retaining/replaying artifacts. Knowing that effect's fields does not establish the phase or actor permission for classic Filch's distinct illicit-taking action.

Classic Filch Super is a different effect on the same card, printed Reveal / As Any Player. Its role question does not test the Wild permission; its different phase makes transferring Super's Reveal restriction to Wild produce a wrong action window.
General flare limits and specifically asked Wild mechanics do not supply a rule that all Wilds are available to every player in every phase. No such universal rule is inferred.

adjudications.novelty_rationale: A player could answer all existing classic Filch Wild mechanics correctly while wrongly restricting the hidden theft to Reveal or to encounter participants. The printed Wild fields permit a bystander to take a permitted item in Regroup. That is a consequential use permission for this action, not another request to recite a card name's fields without changing an allowed outcome.

bounded_proposal.form: Append one bounded permission clause to mutable Q146; no new ID assigned and no bank file changed.
bounded_proposal.proposed_clause: Under its printed role and phase permissions, may an uninvolved player perform the classic Filch Wild cheating action during another player's Regroup?

minimal_required_facts.text: As Any Player: the user need not be a main player or ally.
Any Phase: Regroup is permitted for the cheating action.

bounded_proposal.equivalent_answer: Yes. Classic Filch Wild is As Any Player / Any Phase.
new_credit_excludes: Item lists, sources, ship destination, reveal/Zap windows, caught cost and pile placement already asked by Q146.
Ordinary alien-sheet reveal timing or unrelated flare exceptions.

adjudications.accepted_scope: Only the uninvolved player's eligibility to play an otherwise legal Cosmic Zap on a power use.

primary_references.section: Cosmic Zap artifact illustration — role field and body
primary_references.source_text: As Any Player; Play this card at any time to cancel one use of any alien's power, including your own.

adjudications.positive_original_base_applicability: Cosmic Zap's original printed rulebook illustration explicitly supplies As Any Player. A bystander holding this original base artifact can act; no optional module or individual unillustrated card text is needed.

coverage_comparison.finding: Asks simultaneous player-effect priority, interruption and whether Cosmic Zap can be preemptive. It does not ask whether the Zap's actor must be a main player or ally.
Human's self-Zap asks target identity/own use in a main-player encounter context. It does not require an affirmative ruling about an uninvolved actor.
Asks the duration of a Zap placed during Start Turn, not who may play the Zap.
Asks whether a power use enabled as an ally or outside its usual phase is zappable. That is the target power user's role/phase, not the Zap-playing actor's eligibility.
Asks whether the player may wait for hidden information or Zap retroactively. The unspecified actor in a timing question does not directly test the bystander-versus-participant eligibility rule.
Directing readers to an artifact's own text for when/how it is played does not specifically test Cosmic Zap's As Any Player permission.

adjudications.novelty_rationale: Reinforcements are participant-limited, while the illustrated Cosmic Zap can be played by an uninvolved player. The existing timing, duration and self-target cases can all be answered without resolving that actor distinction. This addition changes which player is allowed to act.

bounded_proposal.form: New unnumbered actor-only question; preserve immutable Q001–Q020 and do not append to Q019.
bounded_proposal.proposed_question: Must a player be a main player or an ally to play Cosmic Zap on an alien's power use, or may a bystander play it?

minimal_required_facts.text: Cosmic Zap is As Any Player; an uninvolved bystander may play it on an otherwise legal power use.

new_credit_excludes: At-any-time wording, the actual-use/nonpreemptive window, interruption rules, own-power targeting and duration are not new novelty.
No claim that As Any Player removes the requirement for a zappable power use.

primary_references.section: Clone flare illustration — Super portion and its role/timing fields
primary_references.source_text: Resolution / Main Player Only; You may choose to receive up to double the normal amount of compensation, if your opponent has sufficient cards.

primary_references.section: Resolution; Compensation; attack versus negotiate outcome
primary_references.source_text: The negotiate-playing main player collects one random opponent-hand card per own ship lost to warp; allied ships go to warp without compensation.

adjudications.positive_original_base_applicability: The illustrated original Clone Super and its fields are within scope, but scope alone does not establish novelty.

coverage_comparison.finding: Explicitly situates ordinary compensation in a main player's Negotiate-versus-Attack loss, counting only that player's warp losses and excluding allied losses.
Already asks the Super's amount range and opponent-card availability while receiving that ordinary compensation. The Super adjusts the quantity of that same compensation event.
The ordinary Reveal/Resolution sequence is already exercised; no separately enabled Clone Super event outside ordinary compensation was found in the allowed printed rulebook text.

adjudications.novelty_rationale: Ordinary compensation is already a main-player Resolution benefit, and the illustrated Super only changes its amount. Reciting Main Player Only / Resolution adds no independently demonstrated legal-actor or timing outcome to Q109's ordinary-compensation case. This review found no positive rulebook-supported non-main-player or outside-Resolution compensation enabler that would make the fields resolve a different branch.
adjudications.rejected_proposal: Do not add a field-recital question solely for Main Player Only / Resolution.
adjudications.reconsideration_condition: Reconsider only if new allowed primary evidence establishes a reachable case in which the same compensation quantity question genuinely leaves eligibility or phase unresolved. No absent-card text or FAQ-only enabler is invented here.

result.conclusion: Accept classic Filch Wild's bystander/Any Phase permission and Cosmic Zap's bystander actor permission; reject a separate Clone Super role/phase recital on the evidence inspected.
result.revision_to_own_prior_review: The previous broad rulebook-only zero-addition conclusion was too broad for these component-specific permissions. This continuation identifies the two bounded gaps above. The prior source/delivery records remain preserved and are not counted as a fresh independent vote.

scope_limits.pending_human_choices: No operational outcome is invented or frozen for reinforcement/Negotiate applicability, ordinary alien reveal timing, Calculator equality or Hate equality.
scope_limits.source_limit: This is an original-rulebook continuation only. No FAQ, native alien image, key, reader, grade or peer-review output was read.
